Houthis launch deadly attack on presidential palace in Yemen’s Aden
item.description:
The Houthis launched a deadly missile attack Thursday on the presidential palace in the Yemeni government’s interim capital of Aden, as Saudi Arabia blamed Iran for the recent dramatic escalation in the long-running war.
Saudi Arabia and the internationally recognized government it backs in Yemen have come under sustained Houthi attack of late, shifting the focus of the wider Middle East war that erupted with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February.
The Iran-backed Houthis have seized swathes of territory along Yemen’s Red Sea coastline in recent weeks, and a government counteroffensive with Saudi air support has so far failed to reverse the gains.
Government military sources in Yemen said at least four people were killed and 10 wounded in Thursdays strikes on Adens Al-Maashiq palace, which also serves as the government’s headquarters in the divided country’s south.
An AFP journalist saw smoke rising and residents of the southern city reported hearing explosions during the attack, the first on the complex since Yemen’s civil war flared back to life in July.
Yemeni information minister Moammar al-Eryani said the prime minister and cabinet ministers were safe, adding the attack had been carried out with five missiles.
A government minister said on condition of anonymity that Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani had been present at the time, but “was not harmed in any way.”
Media affiliated with the Houthis said they had targeted “the headquarters of military operations, led by Saudi officers, at the Al-Maashiq Palace in Aden, as well as weapons depots belonging to them.”
Yemen’s civil war -- in which Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition supporting the government since 2015 -- reignited after the collapse of a years-long truce, with the Houthis going on to launch their lightning offensive in September.
Riyadh on Thursday accused Iran of encouraging the escalation, saying it continued to arm and train the group.
Saudi Arabia’s deputy minister for public diplomacy at the foreign ministry said Riyadh was still in touch with Iran, but that Tehran did not appear ready to make concessions.
“We think that the escalation by the Houthis at this latest stage of the conflict is encouraged by Iran,” said Dr Rayed Krimly.
The Saudi-led coalition said drones fired by the Houthis at the kingdom’s southern region and the city of Khamis Mushait were intercepted.
Yemeni government forces said the Houthis had also fired “several ballistic missiles” at the central city of Marib, which sits in a strategic oil-rich region.
In 2023, regional rivals Iran and Saudi Arabia reached a deal mediated by China to thaw a longstanding freeze in ties, but the latest violence might threaten to upend the entente.
The Saudi ministry official went on to accuse the Houthis of refusing to meet as fighting ramped up between the two sides.
“At the beginning of this escalation, we asked them to meet in Muscat, Oman and they refused,” he added.
The ministry later said that the exchange took place in July.
Saudi Arabia suffered its deadliest attack in more than a decade on Saturday when a strike on Riyadh’s international airport killed 13 people and wounded around 300 others.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said the group had attacked Riyadh’s airport 20 times this month.
Coalition spokesman Turki Al-Malki said “The Houthis must immediately cease all terrorist operations targeting civilians and civilian facilities, including airports, ports, oil facilities, and infrastructure.”
He added the group had “worked to obtain advanced technologies with the help of regional actors,” saying they now had “ballistic missiles, attack and suicide drones, and fast explosive-laden boats.”
The attacks on Saudi Arabia have tested the country’s infrastructure and resilience, the energy minister acknowledged earlier this week.
Riyadh usually hosts a packed calendar of events this time of year, including its flagship investment conference drawing foreign leaders and business titans.
In Yemen, the conflict has caused what the United Nations calls one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises, leaving most of the nation’s population dependent on aid.

item.title: Bangladesh ranks 84th in Global Hunger Index 2026
item.description:
Bangladesh ranked 84th in the Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2026, scoring 19.2 and remaining in the “moderate” hunger category, as child undernutrition continues to pose a significant public health challenge despite progress in reducing stunting over the past 2 decades.
The index shows that 8.2% of Bangladesh’s population is undernourished, while 24% of children under 5 suffer from stunting, or low height for their age.
Another 12.9% of children under 5 experience wasting, or low weight for their height, and 3% of children die before reaching the age of 5.
Bangladesh performed better than India and Pakistan but lagged behind Nepal in the regional comparison.
India ranked 100th with a score of 24.1, while Pakistan placed 106th with 25.5, putting both countries in the “serious” hunger category. Nepal ranked 72nd with a score of 14.5, remaining in the “moderate” category.
A lower GHI score indicates lower levels of hunger and undernutrition, although rankings also depend on the performance of other countries included in the assessment.
One of Bangladesh’s most notable achievements is the reduction in child stunting over the past 2 decades.
The proportion of children under 5 affected by stunting fell from 54.9% in 2000 to 24% in the latest assessment, a decline of 30.9 percentage points.
However, the continued prevalence of wasting among nearly 13% of children under 5 highlights the need to address both chronic and acute malnutrition.
Stunting reflects long-term nutritional deprivation and can affect physical growth, cognitive development and educational outcomes. Wasting, meanwhile, is associated with inadequate nutrition and illness and can increase the risk of death among young children.
Public health experts say improvements in food availability alone are not enough to eliminate malnutrition. Dietary diversity, maternal nutrition, access to safe water and sanitation, health care services and household purchasing power also play crucial roles.
Speaking to Dhaka Tribune, Dr Mehbuba Nur Protha, district technical coordinator at FIVDB, said: “Although Bangladesh has made significant progress in reducing child stunting, the high prevalence of child wasting remains a serious concern, which underscores the need to strengthen maternal and child health and nutrition services at primary health care centers, ensure access to affordable, diverse diets, and improve access to safe water, sanitation, and health care, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized communities.”
The findings come amid wider concerns over the impact of economic pressures, climate-related disasters and disruptions to food systems on household food security.
For low-income families, rising food prices can make it difficult to maintain a balanced diet, even when staple foods remain available. Households may prioritize rice and other inexpensive staples over protein-rich foods, fruits, vegetables and other nutrient-dense items.
Nutrition specialists say children, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers are particularly vulnerable when households cannot afford diverse and nutritious diets.
Dr Khondaker Golam Moazzem, research director of the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD), said: “Rising food prices and stagnant household purchasing power can force low-income families to compromise on dietary diversity, making nutritious food increasingly unaffordable and worsening the risk of child malnutrition.”
Climate change is another concern, particularly for communities exposed to floods, cyclones, river erosion and salinity intrusion. Such hazards can damage crops, disrupt food supply chains, reduce household incomes and undermine access to safe drinking water.
Experts working on climate resilience and food security could help assess how these risks affect nutrition among children and vulnerable communities.
The 2026 report warns that global hunger is rising again, with conflict, climate shocks and economic crises threatening food security.
The GHI uses 4 indicators to assess hunger: undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and under-5 mortality. Together, they capture both the availability of adequate food and the nutritional and health outcomes associated with hunger.
The index is published annually by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe, with research support from the Institute for International Law of Peace and Armed Conflict (IFHV).
Under the index’s classification system, scores below 10 indicate low hunger; scores from 10 to 19.9 indicate moderate hunger; scores from 20 to 34.9 indicate serious hunger; scores from 35 to 49.9 indicate alarming hunger; and scores of 50 or above indicate extremely alarming hunger.
Bangladesh’s score of 19.2 places it near the upper end of the moderate category, underscoring the need for sustained action to improve nutrition outcomes.
Nutrition experts say Bangladesh needs stronger coordination between food security, public health, social protection, agriculture and climate adaptation programs to make further progress.
Measures could include expanding nutrition services for mothers and young children, improving access to affordable protein-rich foods, strengthening school and community nutrition programs, and supporting climate-resilient agriculture.
Better targeting of social safety-net programs and improved monitoring of child growth could also help identify vulnerable households and direct assistance where it is most needed.
While the reduction in stunting represents substantial progress, the latest figures indicate that Bangladesh still faces significant challenges in ensuring that all children receive adequate and nutritious food.
The country’s performance in future assessments will depend not only on food availability but also on whether vulnerable households can afford diverse diets and access the health care, sanitation and social support necessary for healthy growth.

item.title: Puja Udjapan Parishad reports 34 attacks ahead of Durga Puja
item.description:
At least 34 incidents of idol vandalism, temple attacks and other related violence have been reported at Durga Puja venues across Bangladesh ahead of the Hindu community’s biggest religious festival, the Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad and the Mahanagar Sarbojanin Puja Committee have said.
The two organisations called for effective measures to prevent further attacks and ensure the security of religious and ethnic minorities throughout the year.
The allegations were raised at a press conference organised by the two bodies at the Dhakeshwari National Temple complex in Dhaka on Thursday morning ahead of Sharadiya Durga Puja.
The leaders expressed hope that the festival would be celebrated peacefully and without disruption, stressing that religious festivals should unite people from all communities and reflect Bangladesh’s longstanding tradition of communal harmony.
They said they envisioned a society where Eid, Durga Puja, Christmas, Buddha Purnima and other religious and social festivals could be celebrated in a secular environment without fear or the need for police protection.
A written statement was presented at the meeting by Shubhashish Kumar Biswas (Sadhan), general secretary of the Mahanagar Sarbojanin Puja Committee.
Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad General Secretary Santosh Sharma said most cases filed over attacks in the previous year had resulted in punishment, with legal proceedings initiated and charge sheets submitted.
“This year, the notable development is that a total of 34 incidents involving idol vandalism, attacks on temples and other related incidents have been reported so far,” he said.
Sharma acknowledged that negligence by some Puja committees had contributed to a few incidents. Citing an incident in Netrokona, he said security arrangements had been maintained throughout the night, but no one was on guard at dawn when the incident occurred at around 5:00am.
He also said the temple's CCTV camera was defective and therefore failed to provide surveillance.
Despite these shortcomings, the local administration had taken appropriate measures, he said, adding that arrests had been made in 11 of the 34 incidents and action had been taken in the others. Some incidents were relatively minor, he added. “We are satisfied so far,” Sharma said.
However, he stressed the need for justice for major attacks against the Hindu community over Bangladesh’s 55-year history, citing the Ramu violence, the Nasirnagar attacks, the 2021 Comilla incident and the attacks in Sunamganj.
“Even today, we are demanding justice for all these incidents and exemplary punishment for those responsible,” he said.
Among those present were Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad President Basudeb Dhar, General Secretary Santosh Sharma, former presidents Advocate Subrata Chowdhury and Kajal Debnath, former general secretary Dr Chandranath Poddar, adviser Bires Chandra Saha, and Mahanagar Sarbojanin Puja Committee President Gopal Chandra Debnath, along with other leaders.
According to the written statement, incidents of idol vandalism and attacks on temples have been reported in several districts, including Sylhet, Rajbari, Panchagarh, Netrokona and Tangail, during preparations for the festival.
The statement also cited a theft at a historic Kali temple in Faridpur and attacks and looting targeting homes, shops and temples belonging to members of the Hindu community in Sunamganj.
It further reported a robbery in Naogaon involving individuals posing as intelligence agency personnel.
The organisations acknowledged that law enforcement agencies had acted promptly in several cases and arrested a number of suspects. However, they stressed that lasting protection for minorities could not depend solely on police intervention.
They called for a broader commitment to secular values and stronger social resistance to communal violence.
“Security for five days of Puja is not enough; security must be ensured for 365 days a year,” the leaders said, emphasising that building a discrimination-free Bangladesh required promoting secular values and ensuring justice for perpetrators of violence.
The written statement said the administration had assured organisers of full cooperation in holding Durga Puja celebrations nationwide. Authorities had promised adequate security, while relevant public service agencies had pledged support and assured organisers that any problems would be addressed promptly.
The Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad has also issued 22-point guidelines to its district- and upazila-level units to ensure the smooth organisation of the festival.
At the meeting, the organisations reiterated their eight-point demands to protect the rights and existence of religious and ethnic minorities in Bangladesh.
The demands include enacting a minority protection law, establishing a national minority commission and forming a dedicated ministry for minority affairs. They also called for proper implementation of the Vested Property Return Act.
The organisations urged the authorities to remove bureaucratic obstacles to the return of vested properties and restore ownership and possession of land to affected individuals within the stipulated timeframe, in accordance with tribunal verdicts.
They also demanded representation of minorities in the government, parliament and all representative bodies in proportion to their share of the population.
Other demands include enacting a law to protect debottor properties, or assets dedicated to religious institutions; passing an anti-discrimination law; and transforming the Hindu Religious Welfare Trust into a foundation.
The organisations further urged the government to issue a gazette notification declaring the three days from Ashtami to Dashami during Durga Puja as public holidays.
According to the written statement, draft bills on protecting debottor properties and eliminating discrimination had already been finalised.

item.title: Expatriates take alternative routes to Riyadh despite extra costs, risks
item.description:
Mamun, a resident of Noakhali Sadar, works as a truck driver for a company in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. After living abroad for five years, he returned to Bangladesh for the first time two months ago.
His return flight to Riyadh was scheduled for October 11, but it was cancelled. He booked another ticket for October 12, only for that flight to be cancelled as well.
With just five days left on his visa, Mamun grew increasingly worried. He finally secured a ticket for a flight to Medina on October 15.
Despite fears over the ongoing conflict, he is relieved to be able to return to Saudi Arabia.
Speaking at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport’s (HSIA) departure terminal, Mamun said: “My visa is about to expire, but I could not leave. I was extremely worried. Finally, I can travel via Medina.”
However, the alternative route means more time, expense and hassle. From Medina, he will have to travel by bus for 12 to 14 hours to reach Riyadh.
“We have already faced so much trouble, and now there is more waiting for us in Medina. Travelling from there to Riyadh will take 12 to 14 hours by bus, with additional expenses. But we have no choice. We have to go, so we are accepting the extra costs and risks. Please pray for us,” he said.
Parvez, an expatriate worker from Manikganj, has faced similar difficulties following repeated flight cancellations.
“We have been through a lot of hassle. One flight after another was cancelled, and I thought I would not be able to travel at all. Now I have to go via Medina,” he said.
With around seven days remaining on his visa, Parvez decided to travel rather than risk further delays.
“I know there are security concerns, but we have no choice. We have to go,” he said.
Al Amin, from Nabinagar in Brahmanbaria, said flights to Riyadh and Dammam had been cancelled, leaving passengers uncertain about when services would resume.
“All flights to Riyadh and Dammam have been cancelled, and nobody knows when they will resume. Our visas are also about to expire. What are we supposed to do? We are being forced to travel via Medina and then take a bus to Riyadh, which will take around 14 hours,” he said.
“If we could fly directly, we would not have to go through all this trouble. But what can we do? We have no other option if we want to keep our jobs,” he added.
A visit to the airport found expatriate workers travelling to Riyadh via Medina, with many whose visas were nearing expiry changing their tickets to take the alternative route.
The Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight to Medina was scheduled to depart at 3:55pm, and passengers began arriving at the airport by noon. As they prepared to board, their earlier anxiety gave way to relief at finally being able to travel.
Passengers said they had to make repeated trips from their villages to change their tickets. The alternative route and additional travel expenses were costing them an extra Tk20,000-25,000.
Despite the added costs and security concerns, many were relieved to be able to leave Bangladesh before their visas expired.
On October 10, Riyadh airport came under attack by Yemen’s Houthi rebels. Dammam airport was subsequently targeted by a missile, disrupting flight operations.
By Thursday, over 100 flights had been cancelled from HSIA, leaving more than 15,000 expatriate Bangladeshis stranded.

item.title: Feed Industry in trouble as prices of raw materials increase
item.description:
Prices of different raw materials used in poultry feed recently increased by 9% to 40%. In response, feed manufacturers have raised the prices of their products by a meagre 7%. Many are not recovering the cost of production. Rising global prices of raw materials have resulted in margins being squeezed.
However, some critics have been quick to allege that the increase in feed price has no rationale other than profit maximisation. They claim that the price increase has harmed farmers, and increased the prices of chicken and eggs.
Poultry feed manufacturers argue that the price increases are not enough to conver their increased costs. As the industry is very competitive, each feed company is afraid that increasing its price will lead to a loss of market share. Because competition is intense, the feed industry operates with a very thin profit margin.
According to the late September 2026 data, the price of maize increased from Tk31.3 to Tk38.8 (per kg), soya bean meal from Tk58 to Tk66 (per kg). Maize and soya bean meal are the major ingredients of poultry feed. Though the price of maize increased by 24% and the price of soya bean meal increased by 14%, the price of poultry feed was raised only 7%, from Tk68 per kg to Tk72.50 per kg.
Other feed materials have also become more expensive. De-oiled rice bran from Tk26 to Tk33 (per kg), rice bran from Tk33 to Tk39 (per kg), and mustard oil cake from Tk36.50 to Tk39.70 (per kg).
The increasing cost of poultry feed inevitably increases the prices of chicken and eggs. Poultry industry stakeholders suggest reducing taxes on the industry to arrest the upward price spiral.
Mosharaf Hossain Chowdhury, president of Bangladesh Poultry Industries Association (BPIA) and managing director of Asta Feed Mill, mentioned that the price of soya bean meal rose 20% or $100 to $530 (per ton) in the international market in August. “The price of feed was increased by Tk2 per kg in late August and Tk2.50 per kg in September. Yet, feed mill owners are making losses,” he argued.
The first increase in raw material prices came when the maize price increased in Brazil and the shipping cost also went up. Moshiur Rahman, managing director of Paragon Agro Industries, said: “Raw material price increase elsewhere or supply disruption immediately affects the Bangladesh market.”
Ihtesham B Shahjahan, managing director of Quality Feeds Limited explained that it requires almost 80 ingredients to prepare poultry feeds and their prices increased by up to 40%.
BPIA leaders told this author that in the budget for fiscal year 2025-26, the rate of corporate income tax for the poultry sector increased from 15% to 27.5%. As a result, the net profit has already become very low, and feed mills must pass cost increases on to farmers.
ATM Habibur Rahman, chief commercial officer of Akij Feed Mill, said that the price of maize recently increased from $235 to $290 per ton. “If prices of all ingredients increase, how can we sell the poultry feed at same price?” he questioned.
Md Anwarul Haque, general secretary of Feed Industries Association of Bangladesh and managing director of Padma Feed Mill, pointed out that the poultry feed industry is imports 65% of its raw materials. “The prices of feeds have been raised only slightly, in comparison to the increases in prices of raw materials. We are in a survival mode now,” he added.
A recent Bangladesh Bank report reviewed the cost structure of a few companies, and calculated the cost of production of broiler grower feed at Tk61.77 per kg, and sales price at Tk69.75 per kg.
Around 150 companies produce 7.5 million tons of animal feeds, 70% of which is consumed by the poultry sector. A large number of informal feed mills also produce an additional volume of feed.
A study by Bangladesh Agriculture University predicted that the demand for animal feed will increase to 10 million tons by 2030 and that the poultry sector will account for 65% of it.

Durga Puja: BGB setting up 18 base camps for security at bordering puja mandaps
item.description:
Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) is setting up 18 base camps and strengthening patrols to ensure security at around 1,800 puja mandaps located within eight kilometres of the country's borders during Durga Puja.
BGB Director General Major General Mohammad Ashrafuzzaman Siddiqui disclosed the plan while talking to reporters after inspecting the security arrangements at the Ramna Kali Mandir in the capital on Thursday afternoon.
He said BGB personnel have already visited the mandaps and contacted puja committees in their respective areas to coordinate security measures.
“Risks of different kinds can arise at any time. We are collecting intelligence, receiving information from various agencies and working to ensure comprehensive security so that the celebrations can take place without disruption,” the BGB chief said.
He said the force will also ensure security at puja mandaps located within a few kilometres of its headquarters in Pilkhana and other battalion, sector and regional headquarters outside border areas, in coordination with police and other law enforcement agencies.
Ashrafuzzaman said the BGB regularly coordinates with the authorities of the Ramna Kali Mandir, Dhakeshwari National Temple and other nearby puja mandaps in the capital.
He said a 24/7 control room has been opened at BGB headquarters to maintain communication with puja mandaps.
The BGB director general added that the “Sharadiya Surokkha App”, developed under the Ministry of Home Affairs, will allow puja committee members and Ansar personnel deployed at the mandaps to contact law enforcement agencies in case of any problem or emergency.
The BGB will take prompt measures as necessary to maintain security and ensure peaceful and festive celebrations, he said.
Ashrafuzzaman also said intelligence gathering, risk assessment and security measures have been strengthened in coordination with intelligence agencies.
During the visit, he exchanged views with the president and other members of the Ramna Kali Mandir Sarbojonin Puja Udjapan Committee and conveyed his greetings to members of the Hindu community on the occasion of Durga Puja.
Other senior BGB officials were present during the inspection.

item.title: PM calls Dhaka’s air pollution a matter of shame
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday urged people from all walks of life to come forward to protect the environment and forests, calling Dhaka’s persistent air pollution a matter of shame for the country.
Speaking at a meeting to review the progress and implementation of activities of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, he also stressed the need for greater public awareness and collective efforts to build a liveable Bangladesh for future generations.
The prime minister urged government officials to take initiatives beyond their assigned duties to protect the environment and forests.
The meeting, held at the ministry’s conference room, decided to identify and preserve the country’s mother trees within the next six months.
It also directed the authorities to ensure regular care of planted trees, monitor their survival through field visits, and explore ways to expand afforestation in the Chittagong Hill Tracts.
Noting that people have limited access to places where they can spend time in nature, Tarique Rahman stressed the need to increase such spaces and encourage people to develop rooftop and school gardens, as well as gardens in different buildings.
He said public awareness is essential alongside government initiatives to protect the environment, adding that greater awareness will make the work easier.
The prime minister also stressed the need for separate public awareness plans to support the implementation of decisions and programmes for environmental and forest conservation.
Expressing concern over Dhaka’s air pollution, he said the capital has been ranking first or second among the world’s most polluted cities for many years.
“This is a matter of shame for the country. Everyone must take responsibility from their respective positions to change the situation,” Tarique Rahman said.
Addressing ministry officials, he said they have the capacity to do more than their assigned duties.
“Your capacity goes a little beyond the duties assigned to you,” the prime minister said, urging officials not to stop at performing their routine responsibilities but to make further efforts for the country and its people.
He said not everyone gets the opportunity to work for the country, and those in responsible positions should make the most of it.
“Allah has given us an opportunity to do something for this country and its people. You may work from nine to five [9am-5pm]. Nobody will say anything if you do nothing beyond that. But if the environment deteriorates, future generations will suffer, because your next generation will also live in this country,” Tarique Rahman said.
He said everyone needs to go beyond their formal responsibilities and contribute more to keeping the environment healthy.
Those seeking change, the prime minister added, should use their abilities and come forward.
Referring to the plan to plant 250 million trees, he said the entire population will benefit if the programme is implemented properly. Collective efforts, he added, could bring positive results for the people.
The meeting also decided that the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change will take initiatives to make up for any shortfall if other ministries fail to meet their tree-planting targets.
Regular maintenance and monitoring of planted trees will also be ensured.
Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo, State Minister Shaikh Faridul Islam, Prime Minister’s Special Assistant Dr Md Saimum Parvez, acting Secretary Fahmida Khanom and senior officials attended the meeting.

item.title: Dengue claims 10 lives in a day, highest toll yet again
item.description:
Ten people died of dengue in Bangladesh in the 24 hours to Thursday morning, matching the highest single-day death toll from the mosquito-borne disease this year, while 1,943 new cases were reported.
The latest fatalities have raised the country’s dengue death toll to 331 this year, while the new cases have taken the total number of infections to 107,259, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the deaths, four were reported in Dhaka South City Corporation area, three in Dhaka North City Corporation area, two in Chittagong division and one was recorded in Dhaka division, it said.
Earlier, on October 6, the country recorded 10 dengue deaths.
Since January 1, hospitals across the country have admitted 107,259 dengue patients. Of them, 101,031 have recovered.

item.title: Govt plans AI-based cancer screening at upazila level
item.description:
The government plans to introduce artificial intelligence (AI)-based screening and testing for breast and cervical cancer at the upazila level to improve access to early detection for women, Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain has said.
He made the remarks while addressing a workshop titled “National Health Protection Authority in Bangladesh: Design and Structural Aspects” as the chief guest at the International Mother Language Institute in Dhaka on Thursday. The Health Economics Unit of the Health Services Division organized the workshop.
Speaking about women's healthcare, the minister said steps must be taken to ensure that mothers and women do not face embarrassing situations or harassment during pregnancy. To this end, plans are underway to transform health centers into one-stop service centers.
He said the centers would offer AI-based screening and testing for breast and cervical cancer. The government plans to introduce these services at the upazila level in phases and at a low cost.
The initiative is intended to make screening and testing more accessible to women at the upazila level, potentially reducing the need to travel to distant hospitals and making the services more affordable. However, the actual benefits will depend on implementation, service availability and costs.
The minister said primary healthcare was being given the highest priority to bring health services to people's doorsteps. The government has drawn up extensive plans to ensure healthcare for the population, but implementing all the plans at once would be difficult.
He said initiatives were being taken to prioritize activities and introduce them gradually through pilot programs.
The minister also stressed the need to expedite implementation of the Health Protection Act and related activities. Necessary steps were being taken by reviewing and coordinating laws from different countries, he said, adding that special emphasis was being placed on health insurance.
Noting that people have to pay substantial amounts out of their own pockets to cover medical expenses, the minister said this placed them under considerable financial strain.
Calling for coordinated efforts with honesty and dedication to address longstanding irregularities and challenges in the health sector, he said the government was committed to gradually delivering improved and quality healthcare at every level across the country.
Director General of the Health Economics Unit Dr Md Enamul Haque and officials from various divisions of the ministry were present at the workshop.

item.title: Faqir Mahbub: Attempt underway to add 300MW from Rooppur plant to national grid by Nov
item.description:
Postal, Telecommunications and Information Technology, and Science and Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam on Thursday said efforts are underway to supply around 300 megawatts (MW) of electricity from the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant to the national grid by November.
"We are making all-out efforts to supply nearly 300MW of electricity from the first reactor of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant to the national grid by this coming November. In addition, we plan to load nuclear fuel into the second reactor around June next year," said the minister.
Underlining the priority attached to the project, Minister Anam noted that as the 1,200MW capacity mega project is a flagship initiative of Russia's state atomic energy corporation, Rosatom, the Russian side is giving it top priority. Teams of experts sent three months ago are working round the clock to meet the project targets.
During his interaction, the minister also addressed recent queries regarding the mobile financial service provider "Nagad". Clarifying the government’s stance, he stated that the government has no plan or intention to sell Nagad.
He highlighted that Nagad is currently operating in a profitable state and assured that steps will be taken to make the platform even more modern and profitable in the future.

item.title: Titumir: IMF, development partners to support Bangladesh's reform priorities
item.description:
Prime Minister's Adviser on Finance and Planning Prof Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir on Thursday said that the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the World Bank and other development partners will support Bangladesh's reform programs in line with the country's own priorities and strategies.
"For the first time, international development partners are clearly expressing their willingness to support reform initiatives based on Bangladesh's priorities," he said, adding that this would create scope for the country to pursue reforms in line with its own plans.
The adviser made the remarks while briefing journalists on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the IMF and the World Bank in Bangkok.
Titumir said that, besides the IMF and the World Bank, the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) and relevant agencies of China and the United States were also extending cooperation in implementing reforms based on Bangladesh's priorities.
Asked whether conditions attached to IMF loans could pose an obstacle, he said the issues would proceed through the established process. The government was working to implement each step quickly and effectively, and remained optimistic about taking effective measures in this regard.
On the IMF's economic growth and inflation forecasts, the adviser said the projections should also be viewed in terms of the potential impact on the economy if the planned reforms were not implemented.
He said differences among forecasts by international organizations were normal, adding that a review of past data suggested that the IMF's growth projections were generally somewhat conservative.
Referring to the IMF's Article IV mission report, Titumir said Bangladesh's growth forecast had been put at 4.7%. However, the government remained optimistic about achieving its budgetary growth target of 6.5%.
He said the reform agenda had been incorporated into the government's election manifesto and would also be reflected in the forthcoming five-year economic strategy.
The government believed that implementing the planned reforms would strengthen the economy's capacity.capacit, he added.
On inflation, Titumir said several factors were contributing to the persistent pressure on prices, including developments in the Middle East and long-standing inflationary pressures inherited from the past.
Reducing the cost of living for ordinary people and protecting vulnerable households remained key government priorities, he added.
The adviser acknowledged weaknesses in the previous social protection system, saying beneficiary selection had often been flawed.
"Many deserving people had been excluded, while others who were not entitled to benefits had been included. Fragmented implementation had also prevented the programmes from delivering their expected results," he added.
Citing a World Bank report, he said deficiencies in effective social protection over recent years had contributed to rising poverty.
To address the situation, he said, the government was pursuing initiatives such as the Family Card and Farmers Card to improve beneficiary selection through scientific methods and ensure that assistance reached the intended recipients.
He said the government was also emphasizing the development of digital public infrastructure to make social protection programs more effective.
Development partners had responded positively to the government's target of allocating five percent of GDP to the social sector and its plan to increase health spending, he said, adding that cooperation to support these priorities had also been discussed.
Titumir said the government aimed to raise tax collection to 10% of GDP by 2030. Restoring discipline in the banking sector, protecting depositors' interests and ensuring accountability across the financial sector were also major priorities.
He said the government had taken initiatives to return deposits to customers of Sammilito Islami Bank to ensure the security of depositors' money.
Measures would also be taken to improve transparency in banks' financial statements and balance sheets and reform the necessary legal frameworks, he added.
Highlighting past financial irregularities, Titumir said common people were bearing a heavy cost due to the plundering of funds from banks and other sectors.
According to him, around $40 billion had been looted from the banking sector.
He stressed that the money belonged to the people and those involved in financial irregularities and plundering must be held accountable.
He said both those who had siphoned off money and those who had facilitated such activities must face accountability, regardless of whether they were in Bangladesh or abroad.
A coordinated effort was needed to tackle defaulted loans and financial irregularities, he said, adding that holding those who assisted financial offenders accountable would help discourage similar crimes in the future.
The IMF and World Bank Group annual meetings are being held in Bangkok, Thailand, from October 12 to Sunday. The meetings are discussing a range of issues, including the global economic outlook, financial stability, poverty reduction and inclusive growth.

item.title: Experts call for mandatory warning labels on packaged foods
item.description:
Public health experts have called for mandatory warning labels on the front of food packages to help consumers make informed choices as consumption of ultra-processed foods increases the risk of diet-related non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in Bangladesh.
They urged the authorities to expedite the finalization of the draft Safe Food (Packaged Food Labelling) Regulations, 2026, which would introduce Front-of-Package Labelling (FOPL) to alert consumers to the health risks associated with foods high in salt, sugar and saturated fats.
The calls were made at a webinar titled “Front-of-Pack Warning Labels on Ultra-Processed Foods: Progress, Barriers, and the Way Forward,” organized by research and advocacy organization PROGGA (Knowledge for Progress) with support from the Global Health Advocacy Incubator (GHAI) on Thursday, marking World Food Day 2026.
The webinar highlighted the growing consumption of ultra-processed foods containing excessive amounts of salt, sugar and saturated fats among people of all ages, including children and adolescents. Citing research, the organizers said 97% of people in Bangladesh consume such foods at least once a week.
Speakers said complex nutritional information printed on the back of food packages makes it difficult for many consumers to understand nutritional quality and potential health risks. Clear warning labels on the front of packages could help consumers identify unhealthy products more easily, they added.
The Bangladesh Food Safety Authority (BFSA) has drafted regulations on FOPL, which are awaiting finalization by the Ministry of Food.
Speakers alleged that various food industry stakeholders had been pushing for voluntary labeling instead of a mandatory system, longer implementation timelines, exemptions for small packages and less visible or misleading label designs. They stressed the need for regulations free from food industry interference to protect public health.
Professor Dr Mohammad Shoeb, a member of the BFSA, said the draft regulations were currently with the Ministry of Food.
“The draft regulation is currently with the Ministry of Food. We have already responded to various queries from the World Trade Organization (WTO) through the Ministry of Commerce and are also discussing with business associations on the matter. We hope the regulation will be gazetted soon,” he said.
Dr Mohammad Mushtuq Husain, a public health expert and former chief scientific officer of the Institute of Epidemiology, Disease Control and Research (IEDCR), said nearly 71% of deaths in Bangladesh were caused by NCDs, with unhealthy diets being a major risk factor.
He said mandatory FOPL could play an important role in addressing diet-related NCDs and called for the draft regulations to be finalized promptly without food industry interference.
Abu Ahmed Shamim, associate scientist at BRAC James P Grant School of Public Health, said warning-based FOPL was the most effective way to help consumers understand the nutritional quality and potential health risks of ultra-processed packaged foods.
Muhammad Ruhul Quddus, Bangladesh country lead at GHAI, said implementing FOPL would help reduce health care expenditure and advance progress toward Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3.4.
M Shamsuddin Ahmed, chief reporter at Daily Ittefaq, said FOPL was an effective public health measure and that the media could play an important role in expediting the finalization of the draft regulations.
Samina Israt, program officer for diet-related risk factors at the World Health Organization (WHO), and Aminul Islam Sujon, a consultant at Vital Strategies, also spoke at the webinar.
The webinar was chaired by ABM Zubair, executive director of PROGGA, and moderated by Mashiat Abedin, a coordinator at the organization. PROGGA Program Officer Shabnam Mostofa delivered the thematic presentation.
Representatives of civil society organizations, nongovernmental organizations, youth groups, the media and various professional sectors attended the webinar.

item.title: Govt forms eight-member committee to improve security at airports
item.description:
The government has formed an eight-member committee to make recommendations for improving security at the country's airports.
The committee has been asked to submit the recommendations within the next two months.
The Cabinet Division has issued a notification in this regard recently.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has been made the convener of the committee, while the civil aviation and tourism minister, chief of air staff, home secretary, principal staff officer of the Armed Forces Division, civil aviation and tourism secretary, and inspector general of police have been named as members.
The cabinet secretary will serve as the member-secretary of the committee.
According to the notification, the committee may co-opt new members if necessary, and its meetings will be held as required.
The ministry of civil aviation and tourism will provide secretarial support to the committee.

item.title: UNDP signs agreements with 12 organizations for environmental projects
item.description:
The United Nations Development Program (UNDP) signed memoranda of agreement (MoAs) with 12 partner organizations under the Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Program (SGP) in Dhaka on Thursday to support community-led environmental conservation and sustainable livelihoods across Bangladesh.
The GEF Small Grants Program, implemented by UNDP, supports civil society and community-based organizations in developing locally driven solutions to environmental challenges while improving livelihoods.
The newly selected projects aim to strengthen community participation, encourage local innovation and create sustainable economic opportunities, particularly for women, youth and vulnerable communities.
Selected through a competitive evaluation process, the 12 projects will be implemented across ecologically significant areas, including the Sundarbans, Cox’s Bazar-Teknaf coastal region, Saint Martin’s Island, Hakaluki Haor, Tanguar Haor, the Chittagong Hill Tracts and the Barind region.
The initiatives will focus on mangrove and wetland restoration, sea turtle conservation, elephant habitat protection, community-based waste management, sustainable agriculture and climate-resilient livelihoods.
Several projects will also introduce circular economy solutions, renewable energy, resource-efficient aquaculture and alternative income-generating opportunities for communities dependent on natural resources.
Speaking at the signing ceremony, Sonali Dayaratne, acting resident representative of UNDP Bangladesh, emphasized the importance of translating the partnerships into lasting environmental and social benefits.
“The real success of these partnerships will be measured by the improvements they bring to ecosystems and to the lives of people who depend on them. Our focus must be on delivering results that communities can sustain long after the projects are completed,” she said.
Earlier, welcoming the participating organizations, Sarder M Asaduzzaman, assistant resident representative of UNDP Bangladesh, highlighted the importance of community ownership and collective responsibility in addressing environmental challenges.
“These agreements mark the beginning of partnerships built on shared responsibility, local innovation and a commitment to sustainable development. By empowering communities to address environmental challenges through locally driven solutions, we can strengthen resilience and create lasting opportunities for women, young people and vulnerable groups,” he said.
The agreements formalize the roles and responsibilities of UNDP and the partner organizations, establishing a framework for implementation, innovation, accountability and sustainable project outcomes.
Particular emphasis was placed on expanding successful community-led solutions and ensuring lasting environmental benefits.
In association with the Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change, UNDP continues to link biodiversity conservation and climate resilience with inclusive economic development through the GEF Small Grants Program.
The 12 new partnerships aim to demonstrate how locally driven initiatives can contribute to national environmental priorities while improving livelihoods and protecting vulnerable ecosystems across Bangladesh.

item.title: PM attends Abdul Hai’s janaza
item.description:
Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman on Thursday attended the namaz-e-janaza of former Deputy Minister and five-time MP Abdul Hai on the National Parliament premises.
A special munajat was offered seeking the salvation of the departed soul after the janaza held at the South Plaza of the National Parliament in the afternoon.
Tarique Rahman also placed a wreath on Abdul Hai’s coffin to pay his last respects.
Local Government, Rural Development (LGRD) and Co-operatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Social Welfare, and Women and Children Affairs Minister Abu Zafar Md Zahid Hossain, Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Aazam Khan, Deputy Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal, State Minister for LGRD and Co-operatives Mir Shahe Alam, Whip Mia Nuruddin Ahmad Apu and other Members of Parliament attended the janaza.
Abdul Hai, a former president of Munshiganj district BNP and an adviser to the BNP chairman, died at a private hospital in Dhaka around 1:30am on Thursday at the age of 77.
Earlier, the prime minister expressed deep sorrow over the death of Abdul Hai, describing him as a tested leader of street movements for democracy.
In a condolence message, he described his death as an irreparable loss to nationalist politics.
Tarique Rahman prayed for the salvation of the departed soul and expressed deep sympathy to his bereaved family members, relatives, political colleagues and well-wishers.

103 Dhaka-Saudi flights cancelled, over 15,000 passengers affected
item.description:
A total of 103 flights between Dhaka and Saudi Arabia have been cancelled over the past five days due to security concerns, affecting 15,779 passengers.
Kawsar Mahmud, assistant director of the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh’s (CAAB) public relations department, disclosed the information on Thursday afternoon.
Of the cancelled flights, 42 were direct services, including 17 operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines, 10 by US-Bangla Airlines, eight by Saudia and seven by Riyadh Air.
Another 61 transit flights were cancelled. These included 22 operated by IndiGo, 14 by Emirates, eight by Qatar Airways, seven by SalamAir, six by flydubai, three by Air India and one by EgyptAir.
The CAAB said the disruption would continue until the situation returns to normal.

item.title: Guardian wins double at Bangladesh Fintech Award 2026
item.description:
Guardian Life Insurance Limited has won the ‘Insurance Innovation Award’ at the Fintech Innovation Award 2026 for its Automated Claim Processing System (ACPS), while its Guardian Accidental Care initiative received an Honorable Mention.
The two innovations reflect Guardian’s efforts to transform insurance services through faster, more transparent claims settlement and affordable, easily accessible short-term accident insurance coverage.
Guardian's Automated Claim Processing System (ACPS) has simplified the entire claims journey by integrating submission, verification, assessment, tracking and settlement into a connected digital platform.
The system has significantly accelerated claims processing compared to the previous process, reducing paperwork and manual intervention while enabling customers to track their claims digitally.
Between August 2025 and August 2026, Guardian settled more than 261,000 claims worth over Tk557 crore.
Of these, 43,032 claims were settled on the same day, while 97% were settled within a week, demonstrating the impact of digital innovation on claims settlement efficiency and customer service.
Alongside ACPS, Guardian Accidental Care is making short-term accident insurance more affordable and convenient by integrating coverage directly into event ticketing and registration systems.
Starting from just Tk10, the initiative provides 24-hour accident insurance coverage with up to Tk50,000 in specified health and life benefits, eliminating the need for a separate insurance application process.
Commenting on the achievements, Sheikh Rakibul Karim, chief executive officer of Guardian Life Insurance Limited, said: “Our focus is to make insurance simpler, more accessible and dependable for everyone. Through ACPS, we are improving the claims settlement experience, while Guardian Accidental Care is bringing affordable insurance coverage closer to people's everyday needs. These recognitions encourage us to continue developing innovative solutions that deliver meaningful benefits to our customers and strengthen trust in insurance.”
The dual recognition reflects Guardian's continued commitment to digital innovation, customer-centric services and expanding access to reliable insurance coverage across Bangladesh.

item.title: Two Bangladeshis executed in Saudi Arabia
item.description:
Saudi Arabia has executed two Bangladeshi nationals in the Makkah region after a court convicted them of committing an “immoral act” inside a mosque, according to the country’s Ministry of Interior.
The ministry announced the executions on Wednesday, identifying the two as Nazerul Islam Abdul Basir and Siti Akhtar, both Bangladeshi nationals, reports AJEL News.
According to the ministry’s statement, security authorities arrested the two following an investigation and referred their cases to a competent court.
The court found them guilty and sentenced them to death under discretionary punishment, citing the seriousness of the offence and the violation of the sanctity of the place and time.
The verdict was upheld by the relevant authorities, and a royal order was issued to carry out the sentences.
The executions took place in the Makkah region on Wednesday, the ministry said.

item.title: Uttara garment workers block Dhaka-Mymensingh highway for wage hike
item.description:
Several thousand garment workers blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway in the capital’s Uttara area on Thursday morning, demanding an increase in minimum wages, timely payment of wages and an end to arbitrary worker layoffs.
The blockade brought traffic on both sides of the highway to a complete standstill, triggering severe traffic congestion on the highway and surrounding roads and causing immense suffering to commuters, long-distance bus passengers and pedestrians.
Uttara West Police Station Officer-in-Charge Khalid said workers from various garment factories in Uttara began blocking the main road in Azampur area around 9:30am.
They later blocked the road near Rajlaxmi under Uttara West Police Station.
He estimated that 5,000 to 7,000 workers were occupying the roads, carrying sticks and other wooden objects.
Police have been deployed on both sides of the highway and are trying to persuade the workers to withdraw the blockade, the OC said.
He added that workers also blocked the road on Wednesday, but police later managed to clear it through persuasion.
Witnesses said workers from different garment factories have been staging demonstrations in various lanes of Uttara since Thursday morning before moving to the Azampur area and blocking the main road.
The blockade caused severe congestion on both sides of the Airport-Abdullahpur highway, leaving vehicles in long queues and disrupting movement across Uttara and adjacent areas.
Hundreds of passengers travelling on long-distance buses were stranded in traffic.
Unable to reach their destinations on time, many got off their buses and continued on foot, while commuters heading to work and people travelling for urgent purposes faced considerable hardship.

1,702 candidates appointed to different cadres under 45th BCS
item.description:
The government has appointed 1,702 candidates to different cadres under the 45th Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) examination, around 10 months after the Public Service Commission (PSC) recommended them for recruitment.
The Ministry of Public Administration issued an order in this regard on Wednesday night.
According to the order, the newly appointed officials have been asked to join their respective offices designated by the cadre-controlling ministries by November 1.
Unless otherwise instructed by the respective cadre-controlling ministry, they must join their assigned offices by the deadline.
Failure to join on the stipulated date will be considered a refusal to accept the appointment, and the appointment letter will be deemed cancelled, the order said.
The ministry also said the authorities reserve the right to amend or cancel the appointment order if any adverse or contradictory information about an appointed officer emerges after the appointment.
The PSC published the final results of the 45th BCS examination on November 27, 2025, recommending 1,807 candidates for appointment to different cadres.

item.title: Indian national arrested at Dhaka airport with 4.28kg of kush
item.description:
The Department of Narcotics Control (DNC) has arrested an Indian national at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka with 4.28kg of kush allegedly concealed beneath Indian saris in his trolley bag.
The man was detained on Wednesday afternoon at the airport’s green channel in the arrival hall. A subsequent search of his trolley led to the recovery of the drugs.
The arrestee, Abhijit Das, 40, is a resident of North 24 Parganas district in West Bengal, India.
Authorities also seized an Indian passport, 2,160 Indian rupees, 70 Thai baht, a smartphone, a boarding pass and three Indian saris from him.
Deputy Director Md Rajiur Rahman of the DNC’s Dhaka Metro (North) office said a special team led by Dr Md Abu Saeed Mia, assistant director of the DNC’s airport office, took position at the green channel around 1pm following intelligence inputs.
Das, who arrived from Bangkok on Thai Airways flight TG 321, was detained on suspicion, he said.
Witnesses and representatives of various agencies at the airport searched the trolley, leading to the recovery of 4kg 280g of kush concealed beneath the clothes.
During preliminary interrogation, Das identified himself as a porter at Bongaon railway station in India, Rajiur Rahman said.
According to the DNC official, Das claimed that an international drug trafficking network operating across three countries recruits low-income people in India to transport drugs from Kolkata to Bangkok. The drugs are then allegedly smuggled into Bangladesh concealed among goods, including Indian saris.
Rajiur Rahman said preliminary questioning suggested the network was attempting to establish a market for kush in Bangladesh.
A case has been filed against Das at the airport police station under the relevant provisions of the Narcotics Control Act, 2018, as amended in 2026, he added.

item.title: CNG driver injured in cocktail blast outside July Memorial Museum
item.description:
A CNG-run auto-rickshaw driver was injured in a cocktail explosion outside Gate 1 of the July Memorial Museum in Dhaka’s Sher-e-Bangla Nagar area on Wednesday night.
The injured man, Md Shahin, also known as Arif Molla, 45, was taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital before being transferred to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital for further treatment.
The incident occurred around 11pm on Wednesday.
Sub-Inspector Md Mahbub Alam of Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station said unidentified assailants hurled two cocktails outside the museum’s Gate 1, one of which exploded. Shahin, who was standing nearby, was injured by splinters.
“After receiving the news, we rushed him to safety and first took him to Shaheed Suhrawardy Hospital. From there, he was brought to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for better treatment the same night, and he is now under treatment,” he said.
The motive behind the attack and the identities of those involved remain unknown, the police officer said. Police are reviewing CCTV footage from the surrounding area to identify the attackers.
Shahin is the son of the late Bhola Sheikh and hails from Salimabad village in Nagarpur upazila of Tangail. He was staying at a CNG garage in Jatrabari.

Messi inspires Miami to playoff-clinching victory
item.description:
Lionel Messi set up a Rodrigo De Paul goal and German Berterame snapped his scoring drought as Inter Miami booked their place in the MLS playoffs with a 2-0 win over New York City FC on Wednesday.
Victory gave Cristian 'Kily' Gonzalez his first back-to-back wins since taking over as head coach last month, guaranteeing second-placed Miami at least a place in the wild card round, with five games left to play.
"I'm leaving happy. Obviously, there's a lot to improve, but we're making progress little by little," Gonzalez said.
Messi -- who had scored twice on Saturday after returning to his club side from last week's emotional Argentina send-off -- was again a dangerous presence, playing a hand in both first-half goals.
In the 20th minute Messi trapped the ball just outside the penalty area and passed it to De Paul, who found Suarez on the byline with a diagonal looping ball.
Suarez rolled it flat across the face of the goal, giving Berterame a simple finish for his first goal since May.
De Paul grabbed Miami's second on a quick counter with the final kick of the first half. Berterame brought the ball across the halfway line and was slightly fortunate to find Messi to his right with a mishit pass.
Messi drew in three defenders then laid it off with the outside of his left foot to De Paul, who slammed it high to the keeper's right.
In a goalless second half, Messi sent a curling effort from just outside the box over the bar.
As the game clock hit 90, Messi played a short corner to De Paul, who unleashed a shot from outside the box toward the far top corner. United States national team goalkeeper Matt Freese made a superb diving save, tipping the ball onto the post.
New York City, on a dire streak of just one win in their last 11 MLS games, at least had a chance for a consolation deep in stoppage time with a penalty.
Ian Fray brought down fellow substitute Talles Magno, who turned sharply away from goal and ran into the defender's trailing leg.
But Dayne St. Clair made a brilliant save, flinging himself low and right to palm the ball around the bar.
It was Inter Miami's second straight clean sheet, after none in their previous 10.
"I really liked how we handled dropping back into defensive shape. We didn't get caught out on the counter and were very aggressive, breaking up plays whenever a sudden transition from them looked likely," said Gonzalez.
"Perhaps our ball circulation was a bit too slow at times, but that's just how the game played out."
Even with first-place Nashville out of sight this year in the Eastern Conference, the win consolidated Miami's grip on second, and home-field advantage into the playoffs.

item.title: PSG 'got lucky' to win City thriller, says Luis Enrique
item.description:
Paris Saint-Germain boss Luis Enrique said the European champions rode their luck to beat Manchester City 4-2 and maintain a perfect start to their defence of the Champions League.
The visitors ran riot in the first half of City's first home game since being found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules as they raced into a 3-0 lead.
Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha were on target in a near flawless first 45 minutes by the French champions.
But City roared back after the break as Erling Haaland struck twice, while they also hit the woodwork twice and were denied by a brilliant goalline clearance by Nuno Mendes.
"We could have lost this match if they scored the chances that they created," said Luis Enrique.
"I think it was a very nice match, but the way they play, it's amazing. We like to play these kind of matches."
Maghnes Akliouche briefly restored PSG's three-goal lead in the second half, while Ferran Torres also missed a late penalty for the visitors.
"We try to win every single match. We try to score. We don't stop if we score one or two goals," added Luis Enrique.
"It's very nice to feel that but I have to repeat, today we were lucky because in the second half we could have conceded more goals."
Enzo Maresca had made a perfect start to the daunting challenge of replacing Pep Guardiola as City manager by winning his first eight games in all competitions.
Guardiola, who won 20 trophies in a 10-year spell at City, made his return to the Etihad Stadium in a show of support after City were found guilty on more than 100 charges of financial impropriety between 2009 and 2018.
But he saw his former players fall to their first defeat of the season despite a spirited fightback after being thoroughly outplayed in the first half.
"From tonight we can learn many things," said Maresca. "Even if we concede two goals (in two minutes) against the best team in Europe, we need to continue.
"I try to continue to learn from the players because I just arrived three months ago, but the feeling at the moment is very good."
Victory took PSG top of the Champions League table after two games, while City drop to 17th.

item.title: PSG beat City in Champions League thriller, Barcola hits Liverpool hat-trick
item.description:
Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain romped to a 4-2 victory away to embattled Manchester City in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday, while Bradley Barcola hit his first Liverpool goals with a hat-trick in a 6-3 win over LASK in Austria.
Elsewhere on a prolific night of European action, Real Madrid came from 3-1 down to beat Roma 4-3 and Aston Villa demolished Fenerbahce 6-0 at Villa Park.
City were playing at home at the Etihad Stadium for the first time since being found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules over almost a decade that have left them facing the prospect of severe sanctions.
That verdict appeared to be hanging over the City team as PSG raced into a three-goal lead just past the half-hour mark, with Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha all netting for the French side.
With former boss Pep Guardiola watching on, City produced a second-half fightback as Erling Haaland scored twice to take him to four Champions League goals already this season.
However, PSG got a fourth in between the Norwegian's strikes, with City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma unable to keep out a Maghnes Akliouche shot.
Donnarumma later made some amends by saving a Ferran Torres penalty, but City succumbed by the same margin as in their last Champions League meeting with PSG in January 2025.
"In the first half we were far superior to a great City side," Paris coach Luis Enrique told broadcaster Canal Plus. "You can think these games are over but it is never the case at this level, and we could have ended up losing."
Back-to-back title-holders PSG have won both Champions League games this season, scoring 10 goals in the process. They face Barcelona next week.
"Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more," City coach Enzo Maresca told TNT Sports.
Barcola, a big-money summer signing from PSG, had not found the net for Liverpool before scoring three times at the Raiffeisen Arena after Ronald Araujo had broken the deadlock against the Austrian champions.
Jeremie Frimpong and Lewis Koumas also netted for Andoni Iraola's side, who were 4-0 ahead at one point before LASK scored three times in the space of 15 second-half minutes through Robert Ljubicic and Florian Flecker's brace.
"Obviously I think he has to enjoy this because to score a hat-trick in the Champions League is always very difficult," said Iraola of France forward Barcola.
- Real late show, Villa hit six -
There was a dramatic denouement in Italy, where a Marten de Roon goal and a Donyell Malen brace had Roma 3-1 up against Real Madrid inside the final 10 minutes.
However the visitors, who had earlier seen Kylian Mbappe score on his 100th Champions League appearance, produced an incredible late fightback.
Carlos Espi pulled one back in the 82nd minute and Brazil forward Endrick equalised before Antonio Rudiger grabbed a last-minute winner for Jose Mourinho's men.
Swiss international Johan Manzambi opened the scoring for Villa against Fenerbahce on his 21st birthday, setting his club up for their biggest ever European victory.
Nicolas Jackson scored twice before half-time, and Ross Barkley bagged a second-half brace including a penalty. Tammy Abraham completed the scoring, leaving the Turkish side stunned.
Fredrik Sjovold got the only goal of the game as Norway's Bodo/Glimt beat former European champions Borussia Dortmund 1-0, while Real Betis beat Porto 3-2 in Spain.
Abde Ezzalzouli put Betis ahead just after half-time, only for Gabri Veiga and Samuel Aghehowa to hit back for the Portuguese champions. However, Juan Hernandez levelled again and veteran Isco got a late winner.
In Rotterdam, Feyenoord beat Como 3-2 as the Dutch side's coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst got the better of Cesc Fabregas.
Assane Diao gave the Italians the lead but Gjivai Zechiel and Anis Hadj Moussa struck for Feyenoord before an own goal by goalkeeper Robert Sanchez made it 3-1. Anastasios Douvikas then pulled one back.
Ukraine's Shakhtar Donetsk were playing at home for the first time at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge stadium, and they marked the occasion with a 3-1 win over AEK Athens.
Lovro Majer gave AEK the lead, but a Pedrinho penalty levelled matters before Vinicius Tobias and Gleiker Mendoza sealed the win to leave Shakhtar on four points from two outings.
Stuttgart won 3-0 away to Slovan Bratislava in the night's other game.

item.title: 107 DNCC residents receive livelihood support equipment
item.description:
More than 100 residents of low-income communities in Dhaka North have received equipment to support income-generating activities under a livelihood assistance project aimed at improving economic opportunities for urban poor communities.
A total of 107 residents received sewing machines, information technology (IT) equipment and business carts at a distribution ceremony held at the Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) Auditorium on Wednesday.
The Livelihoods Support for Urban Poor Communities in Bangladesh (LSUPCB) project is implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in partnership with the Local Government Division (LGD), under the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives, with financing from the Global Development Fund (GDF) under China's South-South Cooperation.
The initiative aims to strengthen the economic resilience of vulnerable urban households through skills development, entrepreneurship support and livelihood assets, creating income opportunities for women and youth.
In DNCC, the project supports 16 low-income communities through Community Development Committees (CDCs). Beneficiaries receive 3 months of skills training, followed by productive assets based on their skills and business plans.
At the ceremony, 36 beneficiaries received sewing machines for tailoring and home-based businesses, 30 received IT equipment for digital services and technology-based enterprises, and 41 received business carts for small-scale trading.
Addressing the ceremony as the chief guest, DNCC Administrator Md Safiqul Islam Khan said: “These assets are not simply equipment; they are opportunities to build sustainable livelihoods. Beneficiaries must use them responsibly to generate income, strengthen their businesses and create a better future for their families.”
Chairing the event, DNCC Chief Executive Officer Mohammad Ashaduz Zaman said: “Skills development becomes more meaningful when people have the resources to put their training into practice. This support will help beneficiaries turn their abilities into income-generating opportunities.”
Yugesh Pradhanang, international technical adviser and project manager of the Livelihoods Improvement of Urban Poor Communities Project at UNDP Bangladesh, said: “Providing livelihood assets alongside practical training helps people move toward financial independence. Our focus is on enabling vulnerable women and youth to build sustainable livelihoods.”
The LSUPCB project operates across 6 cities and towns in Bangladesh, supporting employment, entrepreneurship and economic self-reliance among vulnerable urban communities.
Mohammad Mamun-Ul-Hassan, deputy secretary and chief social welfare and slum development officer at DNCC, delivered the welcome address.
Through government and development partnerships, the initiative seeks to strengthen household incomes, promote small-scale entrepreneurship and create sustainable economic opportunities for urban poor communities.

item.title: Durga Puja preparations going on in full swing in Tangail
item.description:
Preparations for Durga Puja are in final stages across Tangail, with artisans working day and night to complete idols and organisers putting the finishing touches to pandals ahead of the Hindu community’s biggest religious festival.
This year, 1,356 pandals will host the festival across the district’s 12 upazilas, 110 more than last year. However, artisans say soaring raw material prices and shrinking profits are making it increasingly difficult to sustain their livelihoods.
Durga Puja will begin nationwide on October 15 with Maha Panchami and conclude on October 21 with Bijoya Dashami and the immersion of idols.
Artisans are racing against time to complete idols of Goddess Durga and her children — Lakshmi, Saraswati, Kartik and Ganesha. While idol-making has been completed in many places, work continues at several others, with artisans painting idols and adding the final touches to meet deadlines.
From early morning until late at night, workers are putting in long hours as preparations gather pace and the festive atmosphere spreads across the district.
According to traditional Hindu beliefs, Goddess Durga will arrive on an elephant and depart by boat this year.
Despite the increase in the number of pandals, idol-makers say rising prices of clay, paint and other materials have significantly eroded their profits. They also say their earnings are no longer sufficient to cover household expenses.
Pradip Chandra Pal, an artisan who has been making idols for 20 years, said preparations were now at their busiest, with workers labouring day and night to finish their work.
“The cost of everything needed to make idols has increased. A colour that used to cost Tk100 now costs Tk150. The price of clay has also risen significantly,” he told Dhaka Tribune.
Pal said he had made 10 idols this year at a cost of Tk150,000 and expected to sell them for around Tk250,000.
“Earlier, we could spend six months without work after making idols for Durga Puja. Now, that is no longer possible,” he said, adding that rising costs and low returns had made the profession increasingly difficult.
Another artisan, Arnab, who has been in the profession for seven years, said the workload increased sharply ahead of the festival, leaving little time for rest.
“We hardly have any time to rest during this period. But the money we earn from painting idols is not enough to run our households,” he said.
The artisans called for government assistance to help them cope with rising production costs and declining profits.
Tangail District Puja Celebration Committee Acting President Chitta Ranjan Sarkar said organisers had held discussions with representatives of all puja committees to ensure the celebrations proceeded smoothly.
He attributed the increase in the number of pandals to the administration’s overall cooperation.
“Police will be deployed at every pandal, alongside CCTV surveillance and other security measures. We hope to complete the celebrations without any untoward incidents,” he said.
Tangail Superintendent of Police Mohammad Shamsul Alam Sarkar said a special security plan had been drawn up for the festival.
Police, Detective Branch personnel and plainclothes officers will be deployed to maintain law and order, he said, adding that the police would remain vigilant to ensure peaceful celebrations.
